question.text: Income from exchange-traded derivatives is usually treated as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Gains and losses from exchange-traded currency derivatives are taxable under the head Profits and Gains from Business or Profession (PGBP) and are deemed to be normal, non-speculative business income, even though physical delivery does not take place. This treatment applies because the trades are executed on a recognized stock exchange. The Trap: Capital gains treatment is reserved for capital assets and (separately) for FPI derivative positions; it does not apply to a domestic trader's exchange-traded derivative book. Income from other sources and salary income are simply the wrong heads of income for derivative trading.
